fact_check_verdict: two validators; award record is the only public source for the GAIA claims, no press coverage found; Haines date corrected to 2020

claims.spoken: N S F awarded the University of Alaska Fairbanks one point seven seven million dollars.
requires: Say according to the N S F award record. Obligated FY2026, equals the recorded total.

claims.spoken: The grant runs six years, from August first, 2026.
Carl Tape leads it, with three co-investigators from Fairbanks.
requires: Name roles only as the record gives them. Do not state what West, Meyer or Grapenthin lead.

claims.spoken: The goal is a digital twin that keeps updating and estimates hazards in close to real time.
requires: Goal and design, not a result. Say aims or plans, never has.

claims.spoken: The team plans to test it on landslides in Alaska and the Pacific Northwest.
It pulls in ground shaking, satellite pictures, weather and groundwater.
requires: Abstract says ground vibrations and deformation, satellite imagery, meteorological data and groundwater levels.

claims.spoken: The abstract says those measurements come from separate systems that rarely work together.
requires: Attribute to the award abstract. It is the applicants' framing.

claims.spoken: Heavy rain can soak a slope, an earthquake can weaken that same slope, and a later storm can bring it down.
claims.on_screen: 3 · A LATER STORM BRINGS IT DOWN

claims.spoken: Part of the plan is fast surrogate models, stand-ins that approximate slow physics simulations.
claims.on_screen: SURROGATE MODEL · FAST STAND-IN FOR SLOW PHYSICS
requires: Abstract: fast surrogate models that approximate expensive physics simulations, coupled to incoming observations through data assimilation.

claims.spoken: It also plans software agents that read papers and code and flag what scientists don't yet know.
requires: Abstract: prototypes research-assisting agents that recommend methods, flag knowledge gaps and generate reproducible workflows. Planned prototype.

claims.spoken: Two partner awards share the title, one at the University of Washington and one at EarthScope.
requires: Amounts: UW $2,209,093 and EarthScope $449,448, found by keyword search of the NSF API. Do not claim no further partner exists.

claims.spoken: In December 2020, a storm dropped at least eight inches of rain on Haines in two days.
claims.on_screen: AT LEAST 8 IN OF RAIN IN 2 DAYS · PER KHNS
requires: Attribute to KHNS reporting, a news figure and not an N W S measurement.

claims.spoken: Slides that week killed two people.
requires: Event is December 2020. Alaska Beacon caption.

claims.spoken: In November 2023, a slide in Wrangell killed six people and blocked the Zimovia Highway.
requires: Alaska Beacon via KTOO. Contemporaneous counts rose over days.

claims.spoken: Southeast Alaska has had four fatal landslides in the last decade.
At Barry Arm, state geologists track a slope of roughly five hundred million cubic meters.
requires: DGGS says about 500 M m3. USGS cites 455 M m3 (Dai et al, 2020). Hedge as roughly.

claims.spoken: If it failed fast, it could make a tsunami with life-threatening waves.
requires: DGGS page gives no wave height. Never print a height.

claims.spoken: Fairbanks is also home to the Alaska Satellite Facility, NASA's archive for radar satellite data.
requires: Page: As the NASA SAR Distributed Active Archive Center, ASF plays a key role in managing and distributing SAR data. Do not say Meyer works there.

claims.spoken: The award names no Alaska slope.
claims.on_screen: NO ALASKA SLOPE NAMED · AWARD ABSTRACT
requires: Absence checked in the full abstract text: it says tests on landslides in Alaska and the Pacific Northwest and names no slope. Say the award abstract names none. Do not say a slope was never chosen.
